newsitem.title: USA: USTR says Malaysia to "graduate" from GSP IN 1997.
newsitem.headline: USTR says Malaysia to "graduate" from GSP IN 1997.

text.p: Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said on Wednesday that a presidential proclamation is expected aimed at graduating Malaysia's special trade privileges next year.

"There will be a presidential proclamation issued in about a week which graduates Malaysia from this programme starting January 1, 1997," Barshefsky said during a Women's Foreign Policy Group luncheon.

Her comments referred to trade privileges given developing countries under the Generalised System of Preferences (GSP) programme. The GSP programme, which has to be reauthorised by Congress, allows products from designated developing countries to be imported tariff-free.
In Kuala Lumpur, a U.S. embassy spokesman denied Washington would be withdrawing Malaysia's GSP privileges next week.
He was responding to queries after a wire service report from Washington on Wednesday incorrectly said Barshefsky had spoken about graduating Malaysia from the GSP scheme as early as next week.
The embassy spokesman noted that previous statements have said Malaysia will graduate from the GSP programme on January 1, 1997 and that there have been no changes to that schedule.

"Graduation" from the GSP programme effectively will mean tariff-free imports from Malaysia into the United States will cease and is a recognition of a trading partner's rise to a more level playing field.
"Malaysia now captures a quarter of all the programme benefits. Malaysia doesn't need it," Barshefsky said.
She also said the United States has asked the International Trade Commission for advice on how to redirect GSP programme benefits to sub-saharan Africa.
